key_insight: Small-radius, high-electronegativity A-site dopants like Ca can simultaneously improve proton transport and chemical stability in BaCeO3-based perovskite electrolytes by weakening A–O bonding, increasing vacancy formation, and moderating gas adsorption.
engineering_relevance: A-site doping offers a practical design route for proton-conducting solid oxide fuel cell electrolytes that can outperform conventional B-site-only strategies in both conductivity and durability.
method: Mechanistic analysis of A-site dopant effects on vacancy formation, proton uptake, and gas adsorption.
Assessment of lattice contraction, impurity-phase suppression, and grain-boundary resistance mitigation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports computational and mechanistic evidence showing that Ca doping improves proton transport while also reducing susceptibility to CO2/SO2 attack and impurity-phase formation.
watch_item: Benefits may depend on whether proton transfer is the rate-limiting step, and Ca surface segregation could alter long-term microstructural behavior in real cells.
paper_title: Role of small-radius and high-electronegativity A-Site dopants in enhancing proton transport and stability of perovskite electrolytes
